title: China's Dancing Grandmas: Public Nuisance, or the Healthiest Retirement? | China Travel Expert
description:
Every evening across China, public squares and parks fill with dancers moving in rows to a loudspeaker. It is called guangchangwu (guǎng chǎng wǔ) — "square dancing" — and it is mostly retired women. Some estimates put the dancers in the tens of millions, even over 100 million. It keeps people moving and connected; it also draws noise complaints and the occasional turf fight, so some cities now set the hours and the volume. Think of it as a free outdoor dance class on every corner. So — turn the speakers down, or let them dance?

★ Expert Tip: If you want to see it, go to any city park or public square around 7 pm. Nobody will mind if you stand and watch, and in many groups they will happily wave a curious traveller in.

在中国，每到傍晚，广场和公园里就排满了跟着喇叭起舞的人。这叫广场舞（guǎng chǎng wǔ），跳舞的多是退休的阿姨。一些估算说人数有几千万，甚至超过一亿。它让人动起来、聚起来，也带来噪音投诉，有时还为场地起争执，于是一些城市开始规定跳舞的时间和音量。你可以把它想成「每个街角一堂免费的露天舞蹈课」。那么——是把音量调小，还是让她们尽情跳？

—
I'm mapping ALL of China — real streets, real history, zero tourist traps.
🧭 Your China Travel Expert | 你的中国旅游专家

Facts verified 2026-11-25:
• Square dancing (guangchangwu) is a mass public pastime in China, especially among middle-aged and older women, done in squares, parks and other open spaces; estimates of participants run into the tens of millions, with secondary sources citing figures as high as around 100 million — South China Morning Post, "Why Chinese love to dance in public" https://www.scmp.com/news/people-culture/trending-china/article/3257417/why-chinese-love-dance-public-parks-even-restaurants-health-socialisation-or-self-expression + CGTN, "China's dancing grannies look to inspire aging populations abroad" https://news.cgtn.com/news/3141544e30637a6333566d54/index.html
• The dances have drawn noise complaints and disputes over public space, prompting some local rules on times and volume — The Star, "China's elderly are square dancing in their millions, but not everyone likes it" https://www.thestar.com.my/lifestyle/living/2015/05/15/chinas-elderly-are-square-dancing-in-their-millions-but-not-everyone-likes-it + South China Morning Post (above)

es.title: Las abuelas bailarinas de China: ¿molestia pública o la jubilación más sana?
es.description: Cada tarde en China, plazas y parques se llenan de gente bailando en filas al son de un altavoz: es el guangchangwu, el "baile de plaza", sobre todo mujeres jubiladas. Algunas estimaciones hablan de decenas de millones, incluso más de 100 millones. Las mantiene activas y unidas, pero también genera quejas por ruido, así que algunas ciudades regulan horarios y volumen. ¿Bajar el volumen, o dejarlas bailar?

pt.title: As vovós dançarinas da China: incômodo público ou a aposentadoria mais saudável?
pt.description: Toda tarde na China, praças e parques se enchem de gente dançando em filas ao som de uma caixa de som: é o guangchangwu, a "dança de praça", em geral mulheres aposentadas. Estimativas falam em dezenas de milhões, até mais de 100 milhões. Mantém todos ativos e unidos, mas também gera queixas de barulho, e algumas cidades já regulam horários e volume. Abaixar o som, ou deixá-las dançar?

id.title: Nenek-nenek penari China: pengganggu umum, atau pensiun paling sehat?
id.description: Setiap sore di China, alun-alun dan taman dipenuhi orang menari berbaris mengikuti pengeras suara: namanya guangchangwu, "tari lapangan", kebanyakan perempuan pensiunan. Perkiraan menyebut puluhan juta, bahkan lebih dari 100 juta orang. Menjaga mereka aktif dan terhubung, tapi juga memicu keluhan kebisingan, sehingga beberapa kota kini mengatur jam dan volumenya. Kecilkan suaranya, atau biarkan mereka menari?

hi.title: चीन की नाचती दादी-नानी: सार्वजनिक परेशानी, या सबसे सेहतमंद रिटायरमेंट?
hi.description: चीन में हर शाम चौक और पार्क लाउडस्पीकर की धुन पर कतारों में नाचते लोगों से भर जाते हैं: इसे गुआंगचांगवू यानी "स्क्वायर डांसिंग" कहते हैं, ज़्यादातर रिटायर महिलाएँ। कुछ अनुमान करोड़ों, यहाँ तक कि 10 करोड़ से ज़्यादा बताते हैं। यह उन्हें सक्रिय और जुड़ा रखता है, पर शोर की शिकायतें भी होती हैं, इसलिए कुछ शहर अब समय और आवाज़ तय करते हैं। आवाज़ कम करें, या नाचने दें?

ar.title: جدّات الصين الراقصات: إزعاج عام، أم أصحّ تقاعد على الأرض؟
ar.description: كل مساء في الصين تمتلئ الساحات والحدائق بأناس يرقصون في صفوف على وقع مكبّر صوت: اسمه قوانغتشانغوو، "رقص الساحات"، ومعظمهم نساء متقاعدات. تقديرات تتحدث عن عشرات الملايين، بل أكثر من 100 مليون. يبقيهم نشيطين ومتواصلين، لكنه يثير شكاوى الضجيج، فصارت بعض المدن تحدّد الأوقات ومستوى الصوت. أتخفض الصوت، أم تدعهم يرقصون؟

fr.title: Les mamies danseuses de Chine : nuisance publique, ou la retraite la plus saine ?
fr.description: Chaque soir en Chine, places et parcs se remplissent de gens qui dansent en rangs au son d'un haut-parleur : c'est le guangchangwu, la "danse de place", surtout des femmes retraitées. Certaines estimations parlent de dizaines de millions, voire plus de 100 millions. Cela les garde actives et liées, mais provoque aussi des plaintes pour le bruit, et des villes encadrent désormais horaires et volume. Baisser le son, ou les laisser danser ?
